title: AI Engineer Path
goal: Go from beginner at programming and AI to someone who can build, evaluate, and ship LLM-powered systems that other people rely on.

modules.title: Getting set up
modules.outcome: You have a working development environment, this repo under version control, and a study habit that survives week three.

lessons.title: How to learn this without burning out
lessons.summary: The study loop, why build tasks matter, how to use this site.
lessons.build: Log your first session and commit the repo to git.

lessons.title: Your machine, your terminal, your editor
lessons.summary: Python, VS Code, the terminal, and why virtual environments exist.
lessons.build: A virtual environment you created yourself with three packages installed and a frozen requirements.txt.

lessons.title: Git and GitHub, properly
lessons.summary: Commits, branches, remotes, and what to do when it goes wrong.
lessons.build: A public GitHub repo with at least five commits and one branch merged.

lessons.title: Your first Python program
lessons.summary: Running code, printing, reading errors without panic.
lessons.build: A script that takes your name as input and prints a formatted greeting, committed to git.

lessons.title: Your first call to a real model
lessons.summary: API keys, the Anthropic SDK, and getting a response back in Python.
lessons.build: A script that sends a question to Claude and prints the answer, with the API key loaded from .env and never committed.

modules.title: Python that AI work actually needs
modules.outcome: You can read and write the Python that shows up in every AI codebase, and debug it when it breaks.

lessons.title: Variables, types, and strings
lessons.summary: The data you will handle constantly: text, numbers, booleans.
lessons.build: A script that cleans a messy string: strips whitespace, fixes capitalisation, counts words.

lessons.title: Lists, loops, and conditionals
lessons.summary: Doing something to many things, and deciding what to do.
lessons.build: A script that reads a list of questions and sends each one to a model, printing results as it goes.

lessons.title: Functions and why they matter
lessons.summary: Naming a piece of work so you can reuse it and test it.
lessons.build: Refactor your model-calling script so the API call is a function with parameters and a docstring.

lessons.title: Dictionaries and JSON
lessons.summary: The shape of almost every API request and response you will ever make.
lessons.build: A script that reads a JSON file of records, filters them by a field, and writes the results to a new JSON file.

lessons.title: Files, paths, and the filesystem
lessons.summary: Reading and writing files without breaking on someone else's machine.
lessons.build: A script that walks a folder, reads every .txt file, and writes a summary index.

lessons.title: Errors, tracebacks, and debugging
lessons.summary: Reading a stack trace, using print and a debugger, handling exceptions on purpose.
lessons.build: Take a deliberately broken script, diagnose three bugs from their tracebacks, and fix them.

modules.title: Talking to models properly
modules.outcome: You control what a model returns instead of hoping, and you know what each call costs.

lessons.title: Messages, roles, and turns
lessons.summary: How a conversation is actually represented in an API call.
lessons.build: A script that holds a three-turn conversation and prints the full message history.

lessons.title: System prompts
lessons.summary: Setting behaviour once instead of repeating yourself every turn.
lessons.build: The same question answered by three different system prompts, with the differences written up.

lessons.title: The parameters that matter
lessons.summary: max_tokens, stop reasons, and the settings that actually change output.
lessons.build: A script that handles every stop_reason correctly instead of assuming success.

lessons.title: Streaming
lessons.summary: Getting tokens as they arrive so your app does not feel frozen.
lessons.build: A terminal chat that streams the response token by token.

lessons.title: Tokens and what things cost
lessons.summary: Counting tokens, reading usage, and estimating a bill before you get one.
lessons.build: A wrapper that logs tokens and estimated cost for every call to a CSV file.

lessons.title: Multi-turn conversations and state
lessons.summary: Keeping history, trimming it, and why the API forgets everything.
lessons.build: A chat that persists conversation history to disk and resumes it on restart.

modules.title: How LLMs actually work
modules.outcome: You can predict what a model will get wrong before it does, and explain why to someone else.

lessons.title: Tokens: the unit of everything
lessons.summary: What a token is, why it is not a word, and why it shapes cost and behaviour.
lessons.build: A script that tokenises the same text three ways and explains where the counts diverge.

lessons.title: Next-token prediction
lessons.summary: The one mechanism underneath everything a model does.
lessons.build: A written prediction of five things a model will fail at, tested against a real model, with results.

lessons.title: Embeddings, intuitively
lessons.summary: Meaning as coordinates, without the linear algebra.
lessons.build: Embed ten sentences and rank them by similarity to a query; explain one surprising result.

lessons.title: Context windows and attention
lessons.summary: What the model can see, what it forgets, and where quality degrades.
lessons.build: Test recall of a fact planted at the start, middle, and end of a long context; chart the results.

lessons.title: Why models make things up
lessons.summary: Hallucination as a predictable property, not a bug to be scolded away.
lessons.build: Produce three reliable hallucinations, then reduce two of them by changing the input alone.

modules.title: Context engineering
modules.outcome: You architect the whole information environment a model sees, which is where most of the quality actually comes from.

lessons.title: The prompt is 5% of the problem
lessons.summary: Why the industry moved from prompt engineering to context engineering.
lessons.build: Take a failing prompt and fix it by changing only the surrounding context, not the wording.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a working prompt
lessons.summary: Instructions, context, examples, and output spec — and what order they go in.
lessons.build: A prompt template with named sections, tested on five inputs with results recorded.

lessons.title: Structured outputs
lessons.summary: Getting reliable JSON instead of parsing prose with regex.
lessons.build: An extractor that returns schema-valid JSON for twenty messy inputs, zero parse failures.

lessons.title: Few-shot examples that work
lessons.summary: Why examples are the strongest signal in a prompt, and how they backfire.
lessons.build: Measure the same task with zero, one, and four examples; write up which won and why.

lessons.title: Assembling context dynamically
lessons.summary: Building the model's input from data at runtime, and budgeting the space.
lessons.build: A context builder that fits variable-length data into a fixed token budget without truncating mid-record.

modules.title: Tool use and function calling
modules.outcome: Your model can call your code, and you can tell when it called the wrong thing.

lessons.title: What tool use actually is
lessons.summary: The model does not run your code — it asks you to. Why that matters.
lessons.build: Trace a full tool-use exchange and annotate every message in the round trip.

lessons.title: Defining your first tool
lessons.summary: Schemas, descriptions, and why the description does most of the work.
lessons.build: Give a model one real tool and get it called correctly on five of five test questions.

lessons.title: The tool loop
lessons.summary: Executing the call, returning the result, and continuing until done.
lessons.build: A loop that handles multi-step tool use and terminates cleanly, with an iteration cap.

lessons.title: Multiple tools and choosing between them
lessons.summary: Boundaries between tools, and stopping the model reaching for the wrong one.
lessons.build: Three tools with overlapping purposes; measure and then fix the mis-selection rate.

lessons.title: When tools fail
lessons.summary: Errors, timeouts, bad arguments, and returning failure the model can recover from.
lessons.build: Make every tool fail deliberately and confirm the model recovers rather than looping.

modules.title: Data and SQL for AI engineers
modules.outcome: You can get, clean, store, and query the data an AI feature depends on.

lessons.title: SQL: selecting and filtering
lessons.summary: The query language that shows up in most AI engineering job postings.
lessons.build: Ten queries against a real dataset, each answering a stated question.

lessons.title: Joins and aggregation
lessons.summary: Combining tables and summarising them without getting the wrong number.
lessons.build: A report query joining three tables, with the result verified by hand against the raw data.

lessons.title: Running a database locally
lessons.summary: Docker, Postgres, and connecting from Python — the foundation for everything from here on.
lessons.build: Postgres running in Docker, seeded with data, queried from a Python script.

lessons.title: pandas for data you did not create
lessons.summary: Loading, inspecting, and reshaping tabular data.
lessons.build: Load a messy CSV, produce five summary statistics, and export a cleaned version.

lessons.title: Cleaning real, messy data
lessons.summary: Missing values, duplicates, encodings, and inconsistent formats.
lessons.build: Clean a genuinely dirty public dataset and document every decision you made and why.

lessons.title: Data quality as a discipline
lessons.summary: Validating data before it reaches your model, and catching drift.
lessons.build: A validation script that rejects bad records with a specific reason for each rejection.

modules.title: Selling what you can already do
modules.outcome: You can identify which of your skills are safe to sell today, scope a piece of work, and put a price on it.

lessons.title: What is safe to sell, and what is not yet
lessons.summary: The line between deliverables that fail visibly and ones that fail silently.
lessons.build: A written list of three services you can deliver now and three you cannot yet, each with the reason.

lessons.title: Consulting: scoping and pricing
lessons.summary: If you go independent: finding the work, sizing it, and charging for it.
lessons.build: A one-page service offering with scope, deliverables, and a price, aimed at a specific kind of client.

lessons.title: Framing projects around outcomes
lessons.summary: Recruiters respond to metrics and deployment, not tool lists.
lessons.build: Rewrite all four capstone READMEs to lead with outcome, metric, and tradeoff.

modules.title: Evaluating LLM output
modules.outcome: You can tell whether a change made your system better or worse, instead of guessing.

lessons.title: Why you cannot ship without evals
lessons.summary: Testing a system that gives a different answer every time.
lessons.build: Write down five concrete failure modes of something you have already built.

lessons.title: Your first test set
lessons.summary: Twenty examples, expected behaviour, and a script that runs them.
lessons.build: A test set of twenty cases and a runner that reports pass rate for your extractor.

lessons.title: Deterministic checks first
lessons.summary: Schema validity, required fields, format — the cheap tests that catch most bugs.
lessons.build: Assertions covering every structural guarantee your output claims to make.

lessons.title: Comparing two versions
lessons.summary: Running A against B and reading the difference honestly.
lessons.build: Two prompt variants scored on the same test set, with a written call on which ships.

modules.title: Embeddings and vector search
modules.outcome: You can turn text into something searchable by meaning, and know when that fails.

lessons.title: What an embedding really is
lessons.summary: From text to vector, and what distance means.
lessons.build: Embed a hundred documents and visualise the clusters.

lessons.title: Choosing an embedding model
lessons.summary: Dimensions, cost, domain fit, and why the biggest is not the best.
lessons.build: Compare two embedding models on your own retrieval task; report which wins and by how much.

lessons.title: Vector search with pgvector
lessons.summary: Storing and querying vectors in the Postgres you already have running.
lessons.build: A searchable vector index over a hundred documents, queried from Python.

lessons.title: Similarity and its limits
lessons.summary: Cosine distance, top-k, and why the nearest match is often wrong.
lessons.build: Find five queries where pure vector search returns a plausible but wrong result.

lessons.title: When semantic search fails
lessons.summary: Exact terms, names, numbers, and negation — the known blind spots.
lessons.build: Document three categories of query your vector search cannot handle, with examples.

modules.title: RAG that actually works
modules.outcome: You can build retrieval that survives real questions, and diagnose it when it does not.

lessons.title: Naive RAG, and why it disappoints
lessons.summary: Build the simple version first so you can feel exactly where it breaks.
lessons.build: A working naive RAG pipeline plus ten questions it answers badly.

lessons.title: Chunking strategies
lessons.summary: Fixed size, overlap, semantic chunking, and what splitting does to meaning.
lessons.build: Three chunking strategies compared on the same corpus with retrieval scores for each.

lessons.title: Hybrid search: dense plus lexical
lessons.summary: Why the pattern that survived in production combines both, fused with RRF.
lessons.build: Hybrid retrieval beating your pure-vector baseline on a measured test set.

lessons.title: Reranking
lessons.summary: Retrieve broadly, rerank precisely: the retrieve-20-rerank-5 pattern.
lessons.build: Add a reranker and measure the precision change on your existing test set.

lessons.title: Evaluating retrieval, not generation
lessons.summary: Retrieval causes most RAG failures, so measure it separately.
lessons.build: A retrieval eval reporting hit rate and mean reciprocal rank on twenty queries.

lessons.title: Diagnosing a failing RAG system
lessons.summary: A decision procedure for finding whether retrieval, chunking, or generation is at fault.
lessons.build: Diagnose five real failures and correctly attribute each to its stage.

lessons.title: Putting it together
lessons.summary: A complete pipeline with measured quality at every stage.
lessons.build: An end-to-end RAG system with a published quality number and a README explaining its limits.

modules.title: Evaluation at depth
modules.outcome: You can run the eval discipline that senior job descriptions ask for by name.

lessons.title: Golden datasets from real failures
lessons.summary: Building test sets from production mistakes rather than imagination.
lessons.build: A fifty-case golden dataset split into core cases and edge cases.

lessons.title: LLM-as-judge
lessons.summary: Using a model to grade output, and the failure modes most teams miss.
lessons.build: A judge whose scores you have calibrated against your own manual grades.

lessons.title: When the judge is wrong
lessons.summary: Systematic optimism, position bias, and measuring agreement with humans.
lessons.build: Measure judge-human agreement on thirty cases and report the number honestly.

lessons.title: Metrics that mean something
lessons.summary: Choosing measures tied to what users actually care about.
lessons.build: Define three metrics for your RAG system and justify each against a user outcome.

lessons.title: Evals in CI
lessons.summary: Blocking a merge when quality regresses, the way tests block broken code.
lessons.build: A GitHub Action that runs your eval suite on every pull request and fails on regression.

modules.title: Agents
modules.outcome: You can build systems that loop, decide, and use tools without going off the rails.

lessons.title: What an agent actually is
lessons.summary: Stripping the hype down to a loop with tools and a stopping condition.
lessons.build: Write the smallest possible agent in under fifty lines and explain each one.

lessons.title: The agent loop in depth
lessons.summary: State, termination, iteration caps, and recovering from a wrong turn.
lessons.build: An agent that completes a three-step task and cannot loop forever.

lessons.title: MCP: the standard that won
lessons.summary: Why every major lab adopted the Model Context Protocol, and what it gives you.
lessons.build: Connect an existing MCP server to a client and use three of its tools.

lessons.title: Building your own MCP server
lessons.summary: Exposing your own tools through the standard interface.
lessons.build: An MCP server wrapping one real capability, used successfully from a client.

lessons.title: Multi-agent patterns
lessons.summary: Delegation, specialists, and when one agent is genuinely better.
lessons.build: A coordinator delegating to two specialists, with a measured comparison against a single agent.

lessons.title: Agent failure modes
lessons.summary: Loops, drift, silent tool failures, and observability for agents.
lessons.build: Instrument your agent so every failure is visible in the trace, then break it on purpose.

modules.title: Cost, latency, and observability
modules.outcome: You can run a system without a surprise bill or a silent outage.

lessons.title: Where the money actually goes
lessons.summary: Reading usage data and finding the expensive path.
lessons.build: A cost breakdown of your RAG system by stage, with the biggest line item identified.

lessons.title: Prompt caching
lessons.summary: The single largest cost lever, and the ordering rules that make it work.
lessons.build: Restructure a prompt for caching and show the measured cache hit rate before and after.

lessons.title: Model routing
lessons.summary: Cheap models for easy work, expensive ones for hard work.
lessons.build: A router sending each request to the right tier, with cost and quality both measured.

lessons.title: Latency and what users feel
lessons.summary: Time to first token, streaming, and where the wait actually is.
lessons.build: Profile your pipeline end to end and cut perceived latency measurably.

lessons.title: Tracing and structured logging
lessons.summary: Seeing inside a running system instead of guessing from output.
lessons.build: Full request tracing across your RAG pipeline, with one real bug found using it.

lessons.title: Knowing when it breaks
lessons.summary: Alerting on quality and cost, not just on crashes.
lessons.build: An alert that fires on a quality regression, demonstrated by causing one.

modules.title: Shipping it
modules.outcome: Other people can use what you built, on a URL, without you present.

lessons.title: FastAPI
lessons.summary: Wrapping your code in an HTTP API that other things can call.
lessons.build: Your RAG system behind a documented FastAPI endpoint.

lessons.title: Async and concurrency
lessons.summary: Handling many requests without blocking on the slowest one.
lessons.build: An async endpoint handling ten concurrent requests, with measured throughput gain.

lessons.title: Docker for your own app
lessons.summary: Packaging so it runs the same everywhere.
lessons.build: A Dockerfile that builds and runs your API from a clean clone.

lessons.title: Configuration and secrets
lessons.summary: Environment variables, config, and never committing a key.
lessons.build: Configuration fully externalised, with a documented .env.example and no secrets in git history.

lessons.title: Deploying to the cloud
lessons.summary: Getting it onto a real URL someone else can hit.
lessons.build: Your API deployed and reachable from a public URL.

lessons.title: Load, failure, and recovery
lessons.summary: Rate limits, retries, timeouts, and graceful degradation.
lessons.build: Load-test your deployment and fix the first thing that breaks.

modules.title: Safety and security
modules.outcome: You will not leak user data or get your system talked into something by its own input.

lessons.title: Handling personal data
lessons.summary: PII, redaction, retention, and what you must not log.
lessons.build: A redaction layer that strips PII before anything reaches a log or a model.

lessons.title: Prompt injection
lessons.summary: Why untrusted text in the context window is an attack surface.
lessons.build: Successfully inject your own RAG system, then close the hole you found.

lessons.title: Guardrails
lessons.summary: Input and output validation that fails safe.
lessons.build: Guardrails on both ends of your pipeline, with a test suite proving they hold.

lessons.title: Failing responsibly
lessons.summary: What your system says and does when it cannot answer.
lessons.build: Define and implement refusal behaviour for five situations your system should decline.

modules.title: Building an interface
modules.outcome: Someone who is not you can use what you built, without a terminal.

lessons.title: HTML, CSS and just enough JavaScript
lessons.summary: The browser fundamentals underneath every interface you will build.
lessons.build: A static page that calls your API and displays the result.

lessons.title: A real frontend for your API
lessons.summary: Forms, state, loading, and errors — the four things every interface needs.
lessons.build: A working web interface for your RAG system with visible loading and error states.

lessons.title: Streaming responses in the browser
lessons.summary: Showing tokens as they arrive so the wait feels like progress.
lessons.build: Your interface streaming a response token by token instead of waiting for the whole answer.

lessons.title: Design that does not look unfinished
lessons.summary: Layout, type, spacing, and dark mode — the small set that makes software look credible.
lessons.build: Your interface rebuilt to a consistent design system, readable on a phone and in both themes.

modules.title: Turning it into a product
modules.outcome: You can run one system that serves many paying customers without their data touching each other.

lessons.title: Multi-tenancy and data isolation
lessons.summary: Many customers, one system, and the boundary that must never leak.
lessons.build: A tenant-scoped data layer with a test suite proving one tenant cannot read another's data.

lessons.title: Accounts and authentication
lessons.summary: Sign-up, login, sessions, and password handling you have not rolled yourself.
lessons.build: Working auth on your app, with a second account confirming isolation holds end to end.

lessons.title: Billing and subscriptions
lessons.summary: Taking money, handling plan changes, and surviving a failed payment.
lessons.build: Stripe test-mode checkout that gates a real feature behind an active subscription.

lessons.title: Usage metering and margin
lessons.summary: You are reselling tokens. Knowing your per-customer cost is the difference between a business and a hobby.
lessons.build: Per-tenant cost tracking and a margin calculation for each pricing tier you offer.

lessons.title: Onboarding and the first five minutes
lessons.summary: Getting a new customer to value before they close the tab.
lessons.build: An onboarding flow tested on a real person who has never seen your product.

modules.title: Capstones
modules.outcome: Four substantial systems that together constitute a portfolio worth showing.

lessons.title: Capstone: document Q&A with measured quality
lessons.summary: The single most requested project in AI engineering job postings.
lessons.build: A deployed document Q&A system with a published retrieval quality number and a written limitations section.

lessons.title: Capstone: an evaluated agent
lessons.summary: An agent that does real work, with evidence it does it reliably.
lessons.build: An agent solving a real task, with an eval suite and a documented success rate.

lessons.title: Capstone: production API with observability
lessons.summary: The system that proves you can operate, not just build.
lessons.build: A deployed API with tracing, cost tracking, alerting, and a public dashboard or README of its metrics.

lessons.title: Capstone: a multi-tenant product
lessons.summary: The system that proves you can build something other people pay to use.
lessons.build: A deployed multi-tenant app with auth, billing, usage tracking, and at least one non-you user.

modules.title: Getting paid
modules.outcome: You can choose a business model, show your work credibly, and talk about it to whoever is deciding to pay you.

lessons.title: Your GitHub is your resume
lessons.summary: What a hiring manager looks for in the ten seconds they spend on it.
lessons.build: A profile README and four pinned repos, each with a live demo or runnable quickstart.

lessons.title: Talking about tradeoffs
lessons.summary: The interview answer that separates engineers from tutorial followers.
lessons.build: Write and rehearse a five-minute account of one real failure you diagnosed and fixed.

lessons.title: Choosing your model: employed, consulting, or product
lessons.summary: Honest tradeoffs on income ceiling, risk, time to first pound, and what each demands of you.
lessons.build: A written twelve-month plan naming which model you are pursuing first and what evidence would make you switch.
